column3: The Hebrew says “with him” of the sons and does not attach “their” to the garments.
The recipient is a pronoun rather than Aaron’s explicitly repeated name.
Moses and Aaron are not named explicitly in the first clause, but Moses is named in the command clause.
The sash is singular, used distributively.
The bull of the sin offering is explicitly named again when hands are laid on it.
The Hebrew says the horns all around without an explicit number four; it then says the blood rather than explicitly the rest.
The slaughtering clause does not explicitly name Moses or the ram.
Moses is explicitly named at the burning.
Ear, hand, and foot are singular with plural possessors.
The ordination offerings are plural and placed on top of the burnt offering.
Moses is explicitly named as taker and recipient of the command.
“With him” is retained at both mentions of the sons’ garments.
